questions.question: Which builder prompt is more useful?

answers.feedback: This leaves the purpose and facts unclear.

answers.text: Draft a homeowner email: site visit complete, quote under review, under 100 words, no invented price or deadline.
answers.feedback: Correct. It supplies facts, audience, format and boundaries.

answers.text: Act as an expert and guess the missing price.
answers.feedback: A role does not justify guessing prices.

questions.question: The meeting notes do not name an owner. What should the action table say?

answers.text: Office manager, because that seems likely.
Not stated, with a question to confirm.
answers.feedback: Correct. Separate a gap from a known fact.
A plausible name is still invented.

questions.question: Which details help a first prompt? Select all that apply.

answers.feedback: Correct. Audience helps shape the writing.

answers.text: An invented example of the desired format.
answers.feedback: Correct. A safe example can show the structure.

answers.text: A password so Claude understands the task.
answers.feedback: Passwords must stay out of prompts.

answers.text: The source facts and what must not be added.
answers.feedback: Correct. Facts and limits reduce unsupported assumptions.

questions.question: Claude adds a Friday deadline that was not supplied. What is a useful follow-up?

answers.feedback: A specific correction is more useful.

answers.text: Keep Friday because it sounds helpful.
answers.feedback: Do not keep an invented commitment.

answers.text: Remove Friday, preserve the supplied facts, and check for other added details.
answers.feedback: Correct. State the error and the boundaries for the revision.

questions.question: You ask Claude to act as a tax adviser. What changes?

answers.feedback: A prompt does not grant qualifications.

answers.text: The requested perspective changes, but qualified review is still needed.
answers.feedback: Correct. A role guides the output; it does not establish expertise or accuracy.
Accuracy still needs authoritative checks and qualified review.
